title: Open localized finite pullback is the pulled-back extension counit
statement:
Let $g:T'\to T$ be a scheme morphism, $j:U\hookrightarrow T$ an open immersion and $j':U'=T'\times_TU\hookrightarrow T'$ its inverse image, with $g_U:U'\to U$. Work on small pro-etale sites and their slice identifications [def-weil-proetale-inverse-image, lem-weil-proetale-weakly-etale-localization]. Let $B$ be a finite commutative ring and use its canonical coefficient maps [prop-weil-pbc-proetale-constant-ring-map] and module tensor pullbacks [def-pur-sheaf-tensor-product]. Write $g_B^*$ for this pullback, $j^*,j'^*$ for restriction, and $j_!F=P_F^\#$ for the extension of [def-weil-extension-by-zero-presheaf, def-weil-presheaf-modules-sheafification], with its adjunction [lem-pur-site-restriction-module-adjunction-exact] and the unit-compatible slice sheafification comparison [lem-cbc-sieve-slice-sheafification]. Define $H=j'^*g_B^*j_!$. If $\epsilon:j_!j^*\to\mathrm{id}$ is the actual adjunction counit, then
$$\beta=j'^*g_B^*(\epsilon):Hj^*\longrightarrow j'^*g_B^*$$
is an isomorphism. Under the canonical identification $H\cong g_{U,B}^*$ from [lem-weil-pbc-localize-ringed-site-morphism], $\beta$ is exactly the canonical localized pullback comparison $g_{U,B}^*j^*\xrightarrow{\sim}j'^*g_B^*$. Its generator formula evaluates the summand indexed by $V\to U$ as the same section on $V$. For the actual adjunction $j_!\dashv j^*$, the unit sends a section $s\in F(V\to U)$ to its generator in the summand indexed by $V\to U$, followed by sheafification. The counit $j_!j^*M\to M$ sends the generator in each such summand to the same section of $M(V)$.

proof.text: Use the slice identifications for $j,j'$ and the constant-ring identifications to regard restriction as evaluation on the slices over $U,U'$. The base-change functor defining $g$ sends $U$ to $U'=T'\times_TU$; its functor on slices is the base-change functor for $g_U$. Apply the ringed localization theorem to obtain the natural isomorphism $\lambda:g_{U,B}^*j^*\xrightarrow{\sim}j'^*g_B^*$. The theorem's localized ring map is the restriction of $c_g$ through the inverse-image comparison. This is the canonical map $c_{g_U}$: after adjunction, both send every constant $b\in B$ on $(V\to U)$ to the constant $b$ on $U'\times_UV=T'\times_TV$, and hence their maps from the constant presheaf, and then from its sheafification, coincide. Thus $\lambda$ uses precisely the coefficient maps in the statement, rather than an independently chosen ringed structure.

source.place: Tag 04J0, lemma-localize-morphism-ringed-sites, statement and displayed formula for the localized ring map.

proof.text: Write $a_F:P_F\to j_!F$ for the sheafification unit. The summand construction and module sheafification give the explicit Hom bijection underlying the stated adjunction: $t:F\to j^*M$ sends $s\in F(V\xrightarrow{\varphi}U)$ to $t_{(V,\varphi)}(s)\in M(V)$, extended additively over the direct sum and uniquely across $a_F$. Conversely $h:j_!F\to M$ gives $s\mapsto h_V(a_F(\iota_\varphi(s)))$. Both maps respect restrictions and scalars because the summand restriction sends $\iota_\varphi(s)$ to $\iota_{\varphi v}(s|_{V'})$. Starting with $t$ returns $t$ on every section. Starting with $h$ returns a map equal to $h$ on every summand after precomposing with $a_F$, hence equal to $h$ by the sheafification universal property. These rules also commute with precomposition in $F$ and postcomposition in $M$. This verifies the canonical summand adjunction, including the inverse verifications omitted in the source.

source.place: Tag 03DI, lemma-extension-by-zero, the two transposition constructions and final inverse verification.

proof.text: Taking $h=\mathrm{id}_{j_!F}$ in Step 2 shows that the actual unit $\eta_F:F\to j^*j_!F$ is $s\mapsto a_F(\iota_\varphi(s))$. Taking $t=\mathrm{id}_{j^*M}$ shows that the actual counit $\epsilon_M:j_!j^*M\to M$ is the unique sheaf map whose composite with $a_{j^*M}$ sends $\iota_\varphi(s)$ to $s\in M(V)$. In particular these are the unit and counit of the sheafified extension adjunction, with no alternative natural automorphism inserted.

source.place: Tag 03DI, lemma-extension-by-zero, transposition applied to identity maps.

proof.text: Every object $V\to T$ has at most one map to $U$. On the slice object $(V\xrightarrow{\varphi}U)$, the direct sum defining $P_F(V)$ therefore has exactly the single summand $F(V,\varphi)$; its restrictions are those of $F$. Thus $P_F|_{T_{\mathrm{proet}}/U}=F$ naturally. Apply the unit-compatible slice-sheafification isomorphism to the underlying abelian presheaf $P_F$. Since $F$ is already a sheaf, its sheafification unit is invertible (its inverse is the unique factorization of $\mathrm{id}_F$). By Step 3 and unit compatibility this is precisely the underlying map of $\eta_F:F\to j^*j_!F$. It is a module isomorphism: $\eta_F$ is linear, and the inverse of a bijective linear map is linear. Hence $\eta$ is a natural isomorphism. This uses the abelian-valued case of the slice theorem, so no assumption that the varying ring sheaf $B_T$ is sectionwise the ring $B$ is made.

source.place: Tag 0F6Z, lemma-restrict-back, the subterminal restriction-back situation; unit formula from Tag 03DI. Slice sheafification is supplied by the cited Mathlib leaf.

proof.text:
Define the canonical identification $\alpha_F:H(F)\xrightarrow{\sim}g_{U,B}^*F$ by $\alpha_F=g_{U,B}^*(\eta_F^{-1})\circ\lambda_{j_!F}^{-1}$. It is natural, with inverse $\lambda_{j_!F}\circ g_{U,B}^*(\eta_F)$. Naturality of $\lambda$ at $\epsilon_M$ gives
$$\beta_M\circ\lambda_{j_!j^*M}=\lambda_M\circ g_{U,B}^*(j^*\epsilon_M).$$
The adjunction triangle is $j^*(\epsilon_M)\circ\eta_{j^*M}=\mathrm{id}_{j^*M}$; Step 4 therefore gives $j^*(\epsilon_M)=\eta_{j^*M}^{-1}$. Substitution yields $\beta_M=\lambda_M\circ\alpha_{j^*M}$. Thus $\beta$ is invertible and, under the specified identification of $H$, is exactly $\lambda$, as asserted. Its generator formula is the pullback of the evaluation in Step 3: $\iota_\varphi(s)\mapsto s$ on the open slice. More explicitly, on a presheaf inverse-image generator indexed by $(V,\psi:W\to U'\times_UV)$, followed by a tensor generator with coefficient $b\in B_{U'}(W)$, it sends $[V,\psi,\iota_\varphi(s)]\otimes b$ to $[V,\psi,s]\otimes b$. The relation maps, balancing relations and subsequent sheafifications are respected because this is the functorial pullback of the linear map of Step 3. This also verifies the formula for sheaf sections without claiming that all sheaf sections are global presheaf generators.
